messages:
maria: quick question — can we standardize how the gateway decides region vs zone routing? currently behavior is messy when a zone goes flaky, and it affects dedicated customers.

kevin: yes. proposal: prefer geo-affinity header (X-Redwood-Region) -> zone affinity cookie -> latency-based fallback -> multi-region failover. keep TTL for affinity short (30m) so we don't stick clients to bad zones.

lee: for dedicated customers we need an override flag so ops can pin them to a region even if latency suggests otherwise. is that the plan?

maria: correct. operator override should be highest priority, then customer-specified region, then inferred affinity. overrides must be auditable in the console and via the API.

tom: how do we express this in the gateway rules though? proto for match order would help.

kevin: thinking of a rule list like: 
```
- match: headers.X-Redwood-Region != null -> route to header.region
- match: cookie.redwood_zone_affinity != null -> route to cookie.zone
- match: latency[region] < threshold -> route to lowest-latency region
- else -> route to primary region for account
```
Also add an `allow_override: true` field per-route.

sophia: telemetry ask: we need counters for "sticky-hits", "header-routed", "latency-routed", and a histogram of decision latency. dashboards should show per-account split.

maria: +1. also add a metric for "failover_count" when we kick to fallback region. alerts when failover_count spikes for >1% of traffic in 5m.

ops-bot: :deploy: rollout started for gateway-config v2 -> canary 10% in us-west1

tom: rollout UX question — console should surface the active routing policy for a given route + preview which requests will be affected. maybe a "simulate" input where you paste headers and see routing decision.

lee: simulation is great. include a raw decision trace with reasons, e.g., `reason: header`, `reason: latency`, `reason: override`. Useful for support.

kevin: implementation detail: latency-based decisions must be percentile-aware (p50/p95) and bounded by sampling budget. we can't compute p95 per-request; use recent sliding window per-region.

maria: quota implications — if we route more traffic to a fallback region we might exceed region-specific reserved capacity. need an auto-throttle or priority buckets for reserved accounts.

sophia: add an event to telemetry when quota-exceeded-by-routing triggers fallback denial. dashboard should show "route_denied_due_to_capacity" with account_id.

tom: question: header name collisions? some customers already send X-Region. we should use X-Redwood-Region to avoid clobbering. document in API reference and reject ambiguous headers when `strict_header_mode` is on.

kevin: also: make header parsing strict: allowed values = canonical region codes (e.g., us-west1, eu-central1). fallback to error if unknown and `strict_header_mode` enabled.

maria: action items: 1) kevin draft gateway rule proto + examples, 2) sophia draft telemetry metrics and dashboard widgets, 3) tom wire up simulation UX and audit trail, 4) lee spec operator override API + audit log. I'll collate and schedule a sync after drafts.

sophia: noted. will include Grafana panel mockups.

kevin: pushing draft to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/482 (will ping once ready).

lee: if ops needs an emergency kill-switch to disable latency-based routing globally, add a feature flag with immediate effect and broadcast message.

maria: yes — emergency flag + runbook. ops-bot, create an incident template for region-failure runbook?

ops-bot: incident template created: "region-failure" -> https://redwood.ops/incidents/templates/region-failure

tom: one last thing — tests. we need unit tests for rule priority and an e2e sim that exercises header/cookie/latency combos. small harness in gateway-test.

maria: great. thanks all. I'll follow up with the sync invite. :thumbsup:
